# wall_effect_resolvable_ceiling@v1

The highest bead-centre height at which the wall still changes the drag by more than the target relative error.

- **Kind:** `bound`, side effect `none`.
- **Bounds:** `bead_centre_height`, side `max`.
- **Applies to:** observables `trapped_particle_drag_coefficient` on `transmitted`.
- **State:** planned: its code and a running case have not landed, so no run can use it.

## Inputs

| input | unit | obtained by | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bead_radius` | um | source | radius of the trapped bead |
| `drag_relative_error` | 1 | person, a judgement | the question's target relative error on the drag, from the goal: a judgement, bound to a row with its own source, and the person may replace it |

A missing input refuses the run before any code runs, and the run sheet says how the input is obtained. Never fill one with an estimate of your own.

## Outputs

- `bead_centre_height_max` (um): the height at which the parallel wall correction equals the target relative error

## Source

Tolić-Nørrelykke, Schäffer, Howard, Pavone, Jülicher & Flyvbjerg, Rev. Sci. Instrum. 77, 103101 (2006). Eq. 40, solved for the height at which the correction falls to the target.

Store entry `wall_drag_parallel_faxen_series`, not pinned yet, because the entry is not in the store.

**Where it holds.** One plane no-slip wall; a second wall adds its own correction.
